mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the 3-month federal funds rate over the next 60 trading days indicates monetary easing, which lowers discount rates and increases present-value pricing of future equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 across any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the 3-month federal funds rate above 4.5% in the next 20 trading days signals tightening, which raises discount rates and compresses expected equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) over the next 5 trading days indicates labor market strengthening, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day horizon 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below -0.5% in the next 5 trading days signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer and business confidence and compresses earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day horizon 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% over the next 20 trading days signals demand softening, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day horizon 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% over the next 60 trading days signals supply-side expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day horizon 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 3-month federal funds rate over the next 60 trading days combined with a sustained rise in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of more than 0.5% indicates monetary easing and inflationary pressures, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day horizon 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of more than 0.5% combined with a sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below -0.5% over the next 20 trading days signals inflationary pressures and labor market weakness, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day horizon 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.
